correctness.rationale: If an initial set contains a spine vertex \(x\) or \(y\), the domination step observes that spine and one internal vertex on every page, after which each page forces through. With no spine vertex selected, any touched page becomes fully observed and can ensure both spine vertices are observed. If at most one page is untouched, a spine vertex then has a unique unobserved neighbor in that page and propagation finishes; if at least two pages are untouched, each spine vertex has at least two unobserved page neighbors and the process stalls. Thus the iff criterion is correct. Counting a nonempty spine choice gives \(q(x)(1+x)^{2r}\) with \(q(x)=x(x+2)\); touching all pages gives \(q(x)^r\); omitting exactly one page gives \(r q(x)^{r-1}\). The package verifier independently simulates power domination on every subset for \(2\le r\le8\), checks every coefficient, the total count, and the minimum-set count.
residual_risks: The formula is for the \(C_4\)-page book with a common edge and does not cover longer-cycle or triangular books.
